webdesk_source_audit.native_codec_fallback: Nested encoder implementations remain H264: NVENC -> MF -> builtin H264. They do not require renegotiation to VP8.
webdesk_source_audit.dart_codec_switch: adaptive_video.dart marks H264 expensive after three CPU-pressure samples, remote_session.dart reorders codecs and offers again, allowing VP8. A hardware flag is not used by the Dart pressure predicate.
webdesk_source_audit.hardware_stats: NVENC GetEncoderInfo reports initialized&&!failed. WebRTC propagates this to powerEfficientEncoder; its own hardware CPU-overuse thresholds are 150/200 percent, but Dart uses an independent 85 percent utilisation threshold.
webdesk_source_audit.recommendation: Choose H264 protocol preference independently of hardware availability; retain same-H264 software fallback. Apply pressure to capture/frame/bitrate budgets, not an automatic H264-to-VP8 codec change. Do not label this as Billd default.
webdesk_source_audit.upstream_failure_boundary: If all H264 implementation initialization fails and switch_encoder_on_init_failures is enabled, upstream VideoStreamEncoder requests an encoder switch (video_stream_encoder.cc:1533-1540); ApplyEncoderSwitch may remove the current negotiated codec and choose the next (webrtc_video_engine.cc:1278-1288). WEBRTC_VIDEO_CODEC_ENCODER_FAILURE during Encode also reaches this path (video_stream_encoder.cc:2215-2220). Therefore a generic failure-level cross-codec fallback remains possible, but hardware unavailability alone does not require it.
webdesk_source_audit.fallback_encoder_metadata: VideoEncoderSoftwareFallbackWrapper::GetEncoderInfo chooses active fallback/main EncoderInfo (api/video_codecs/video_encoder_software_fallback_wrapper.cc:458-465). It does not pin a stale hardware flag.
